overview: Spicy's Bhop is a seven-mode bunny-hop module: a vanilla auto-jump mode, a PvpLands mode with double jumps and a 0.035 air drift, two noClip-based speed modes (Hypixel and Test) that re-pin the horizontal velocity to its own magnitude plus a per-tick increment while accelerating the client timer, and an NCP-style strafe mode (Test 3) built on the classic 0.2873 speed base with the 0.42 jump and a 1/165 air decay. The Hypixel Speed NumberSetting (default 0.01, range 0.0001 to 0.03) is added to the settings list only while a Hypixel-family mode is active. A lagback guard counts S08PacketPlayerPosLook teleports and disables the module after three within a five-second window. One registered mode, Test 2, has no branch in any handler, so selecting it runs nothing.

sections.p: Vanilla is a pure auto-bhop: on ground, the module clears the jump keybind, calls thePlayer.jump() and forces sprint, producing a legal jump every ground tick. PvpLands doubles the jump on ground and, in the air, subtracts sin(yaw) times 0.035 from motionX and adds cos(yaw) times 0.035 to motionZ each tick, a small air-control drift. Hypixel and Test both set thePlayer.noClip = true, jump at the fine ground probe, re-pin the horizontal velocity to the current magnitude plus the Speed increment via MovementUtils.setMotion, and differ only in the air vertical: Hypixel leaves it to the timer, Test writes motionY = -0.01 plus a small random. Test 3 is the NCP-style mode: on ground it writes motionY 0.41999998688697815 and sets the speed accumulator to 0.2873 times 2.15, in air it decays the accumulator by speed/165 each tick, and every tick it re-pins motion to max(speed, forward) with a 1e-5 to 9.9e-4 random y jitter on ground ticks.

Three modes raise mc.timer.ticksPerSecond while airborne: Hypixel and Test switch to 26.5 plus a random float whenever the player is not on ground at the 1-block probe and fall distance is under 1.5, and Test 3 uses the same ladder with the threshold at fall distance 3. On the ground the timer snaps back to 20. The result is a sustained 26.5-plus ticks per second while hopping, which scales the whole C03 stream: the server sees roughly 26.5 or more movement packets per second instead of 20, and each accelerated tick carries a full sprint step, so the reported speed compounds with the timer.

The S08 guard turns the module into a retreat-on-lagback design. Every incoming S08PacketPlayerPosLook increments lagbackCheck; at three teleports the module disables itself with a warning notification and resets lastLagback to five seconds in the past, which re-arms the counting window. The update handler clears the counter whenever five seconds pass without a teleport, then re-arms the window for ten more. The intent is to stop before a sustained violation stream accumulates, which is a self-disable, not a bypass.

files.label: Bhop.java (module)
files.explanation:
All logic lives in the module file: the mode dispatch runs in the EventMotion before-post branch, the S08 guard in the EventPacket pre branch, the lagback window reset in EventUpdate, and the Test 3 strafe model in a separate EventMove branch that fires before the pre phase. The onSettingChange handler attaches the hypixelSpeed setting only while a Hypixel-family mode is selected, and onEnable refuses to run alongside the client's Fly module, toggling itself off with a warning. onDisable restores ticksPerSecond and timerSpeed to 20 and 1.0.

Test 3 is the most interesting branch: the event y write (motionY 0.41999998688697815) is the exact vanilla jump velocity, the speed base 0.2873 times 2.15 is the classic NCP bunny-hop ceiling, and the air decay divides by 165 instead of the usual 159.9, a slightly gentler curve tuned against NCP's friction model. The mode also writes event.setSpeed(Math.max(this.speed, speed)), where the second operand is the same field, a redundant self-assignment, and the Test 2 mode string is registered but matched nowhere.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (motion writers)
files.explanation:
The speed modes all route through MovementUtils.setMotion(double), which resolves the movement input into a yaw, applies the 45-degree diagonal blend, and writes motionX and motionZ as forward times speed times the yaw components. Called with the current horizontal magnitude plus the Speed increment, it preserves the existing direction while adding to the magnitude, which is how the per-tick boost compounds without the client changing heading.

isOnGround(double) is the ground probe the modes key on: it offsets the bounding box down by the given height and checks for collisions, so the 0.00004 probe in Hypixel and Test treats the player as grounded the moment the box touches anything within a hair, while the 1.0 probe used for the timer ladder measures a full-block clearance. The same class serves AntiVoid and the rest of the movement family.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly's horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation, which predicts the per-tick distance from walk speed, sprint state and potions: on a stock 1.8.9 server the sprint prediction is roughly 0.31 blocks per tick, and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) plus max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100 with a set-back. Ground state is ray-traced from the block cache, so the noClip true flag the Hypixel and Test modes set means nothing to the check.

Test 3 is the direct target: the 0.6177 blocks-per-tick air pin (0.2873 times 2.15) sits about 0.3 above the sprint prediction, so every air tick contributes hDistanceAboveLimit near 0.3 and the violation accumulates past 30 per tick before the decay can bring the speed down. The Hypixel and Test modes compound worse: each air tick re-pins to the current magnitude plus up to 0.03, so the speed climbs without bound, and the accelerated timer multiplies the number of offending ticks per second. The 0.42 jump itself passes the vertical side (NCP grants a jumpDelay window of 10 ticks), but the horizontal pin is what the envelope measures.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
MorePackets counts serverbound move packets content-blind. MovingListener invokes the check on every processed move, each scored into data.morePacketsFreq, an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets, against a window ceiling of 22 packets per second with 20 ideal, plus a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (15 packets default, direct violation at 10) and lag adaption. A violation returns the set-back location seeded from the SurvivalFly set-back.

The timer acceleration is what this check sees. With ticksPerSecond at 26.5 plus a random float in air, the hop stream sustains roughly 26.5 or more C03s per second, which is above the 22/s ceiling: the window accumulator runs positive for as long as the player stays airborne, tagging epsacc and cancelling at the violation threshold. Because the check is content-blind, the noClip flag and the speed increments give no cover, and the random timer float only changes how far over the ceiling the stream runs.

countering.label: Speed (horizontal stage table)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Speed check stages the allowed horizontal speed by vertical state. Off ground the expectation is getBaseMoveSpeed (0.2873) plus a stage chosen from the vertical delta: 0.049 when vertical is zero, 0.08 when below 0.34, 0.3261 at or above 0.34. On ground, once groundTicks reaches 5, the expected value becomes thisMove divided by groundTime (capped at 8) plus the base move, and the fail carries the BunnyHop label.

Test 3's 0.6177 air pin exceeds every stage: on the rising ticks the expected 0.6134 is beaten by a hair, and on every descending tick the expected 0.3673 is beaten by about 0.25, so the BunnyHop violation fires on the first descent. The Hypixel and Test modes' compounding re-pin crosses the same table within a few air ticks. The 0.42 jump's rising phase is the one legal window, exactly as the stage table is designed: a vanilla jump with a vanilla speed passes, and the module's pinned speed does not.

countering.label: Speed (momentum conservation)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Speed check conserves momentum: the expected speed is friction times the previous speed times any multipliers (soul sand, web, hit slowdown), plus the adders, of which the only relevant one is the +0.2 vanilla sprint-jump boost. The discrepancy between reported and expected speed accumulates per player, and once the total passes the 0.1 threshold the player is punished with a rubberband, with the violation level growing by discrepancy times 10.

The sprint-jump adder forgives exactly the vanilla jump pattern, and none of the modes produce it. PvpLands' double jump adds a second 0.42 launch per ground tick, the Hypixel and Test modes re-pin the magnitude above the momentum model every tick so the discrepancy never decays, and Test 3's 0.6177 pin beats the expected roughly 0.31 by about 0.3 per move, crossing the 0.1 threshold on the first air tick. The module's own S08 guard acknowledges the outcome: on a server with checks like these, the third teleport disables it.
